data.name: Amrendra
data.gender_notes: Amrendra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Amrendra is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Amar' (Immortal) and 'Ratra' (Night). The name signifies the one who is the lord of the earth, who rules over the night and is immortal. The name Amrendra carries the meaning “Lord of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amrendra usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Amrendra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amrendra total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Amrendra holds significant status in Indian mythology and is associated with several revered Hindu deities. One of the most notable is Lord Shiva, who is often referred to as 'Rudra' - the god of rains and the lord of the night sky. The name Amrendra can also be seen in the names of other gods such as 'Amritesvara', the god of nectar and prosperity, and 'Amreshwara', the local god of water in ancient Indian cultures.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, the name Amrendra signifies the eternal and indestructible nature of the divine consciousness. It represents the supreme power that rules over the cycles of life and death, the night and day, and the material and spiritual realms. The name serves as a constant reminder of the timeless and all-pervading presence of the divine, invoking feelings of awe, reverence, and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amrendra: Radiant with the infinite love of Lord Ama (Rama). The name signifies the inner awakening to the divine love and the constant quest for spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Amrendra Chandra was a Bengali poet and philosopher of the 19th century, who is known for his works on the Bhagavad Gita and Advaita Vedanta. He was also a prominent figure in the Brahmo Samaj, a Hindu reformist movement that sought to revitalize Hinduism through a return to its ancient roots.

Amrendra Mohun Sangitkar was a 17th-century musician and composer in the royal courts of Bengal. He is considered to be one of the pioneers of the Hindustani classical music tradition, and is known for his compositions in the raga Bhimpalasi.
